messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Minimum apogee is 250 m. Has to land softer than 4.5 m/s. Total impulse has to stay under 40 N-s. We've got a 1 m rod to work with.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee at least 250 m (minimum). Landing softer than 4.5 m/s (maximum). Total impulse under 40 N*s (maximum, strict). Rail is 1 m (fixed). Wind and launch angle are not stated: I assume 2 m/s wind, vertical, sea level. Single stage. A 1 m rod is short, so the motor has to be punchy as well as under 40 N*s.

2. Feasibility: Drag-free speed for 250 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 250) = 70 m/s, so a D or a small E is enough impulse. Off a 1 m rail, 15 m/s needs an average acceleration near 15^2 / (2 * 1) = 112 m/s^2 before gravity is even added, which points at a high-thrust D or E rather than a long-burn. Looking those up.

2. Feasibility: E30 is 33.6 N*s, under the 40 N*s cap, with 34.9 N average and a 49 N peak in 0.96 s. D12 is only 10.4 N and will struggle to reach 15 m/s on a 1 m rod. E12 is 27.1 N*s but only 11.2 N average, same problem. E20W is 34.7 N*s at 22 N, legal but softer off the rod than the E30. D21T is 19.6 N*s, which may not clear 250 m once the rocket has any size. E30-7 is the one that satisfies both the impulse cap and the short rod.

3. Size: Liftoff guess 0.09 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 34.9 / (0.09 * 9.81) = 39.5. Weight is 0.09 * 9.81 = 0.883 N, rail acceleration (34.9 - 0.88) / 0.09 = 378 m/s^2, rail exit sqrt(2 * 378 * 1) = 27.5 m/s. Burnout mass is about 0.09 - 0.018 = 0.072 kg. For a 4 m/s sink, under the 4.5 m/s cap, a 0.40 m chute is enough. Delay 7 s: burnout is under 1 s, and a flight past 250 m should still be coasting at 8 s.

4. Draft: 34 mm cardboard, 0.35 m tube, short ogive, three balsa fins, 24 mm mount, E30-7, 0.40 m chute on ejection. Rail length 1 m, wind left at the 2 m/s default.

4. Check: The simulator gives 583.6 m, well above the 250 m minimum. Total impulse is 33.6 N*s, under 40 N*s. Landing is 3.6 m/s, softer than 4.5 m/s. Rail exit on the 1 m rod is 30.3 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 35.6, and margin is 1.03 cal at rail exit and through the burn. The chute opens at 8.0 s, just before the 8.21 s apogee, at 2.8 m/s. No warnings. Liftoff mass is 0.1 kg, close to the 0.09 kg guess.

5. Fix: no change needed; the minimum altitude, the impulse cap and the gates all pass.

6. Uncertainty: Margin is only 1.03 cal, so a heavier nose or a fin that comes out smaller will go unstable before the altitude becomes a problem. 583.6 m is far above 250 m, and that extra height is sensitive to drag and to the real mass around 0.1 kg. The 7 s delay is matched to this light build; a heavier one will still be climbing at ejection. Chute Cd is 0.8. Landing at 3.6 m/s has some room under 4.5 m/s, but not if the canopy is smaller than 0.40 m.
messages.content:
E30-7 in a 34 mm cardboard rocket, three balsa fins, 0.40 m chute.
The simulator gives 583.6 m on a 1 m rail, above the 250 m minimum, impulse 33.6 N*s under 40 N*s.
Landing 3.6 m/s, margin 1.03 cal, rail exit 30.3 m/s.
